shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures ended higher on Tuesday, supported by strength in soybeans and wheat that helped to offset seasonal U.S. harvest pressure, traders said.

children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures ended higher on Tuesday, supported by strength in soybeans and wheat that helped to offset seasonal U.S. harvest pressure, traders said.
A jump in crude oil prices
tied to supply disruptions in the Middle East lent additional support to soybeans and corn, both of which are used in the production of biofuels.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) ended up 2-1/2 cents at $5.35-3/4 per bushel but stayed inside of Monday's trading range.
Harvesting was under way in the U.S. Midwest, although heavy rains were stalling field work in parts of Iowa, the top U.S. corn state.
The USDA on Monday reported U.S. corn harvest progress as 8% complete, ahead of the five-year average of 6%.
Brazilian crop agency Conab projected the country's total 2026/27 corn production at a record 148 million tons, above USDA's Brazil forecast for 139 million tons.
